faq.q: What is the origin of Shakeel?
faq.a: Shakeel is associated with Arabic. Shakeel is Arabic شَكِيل (Shakīl), meaning 'handsome, well-formed'.
Yes — the underlying form شَكِيل is Arabic.
Shakeel can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shakeel should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Shakīl is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Shakeel mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Shakeel is rendered شکیل and carries the sense شکیل، خوش‌اندام.
A romanized syllable approximation is sha-keel. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Shakeel?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Shakeel, shakeel. Script forms are شَكِيل, شکيل, شکیل, शकील.

faq.q: Is Shakeel a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
